paragraphs.text: Take heed that ye do not your righteousness before men, to be seen of them: else ye have no reward with your Father who is in heaven.
paragraphs.original: Προσέχετε δὲ τὴν δικαιοσύνην ὑμῶν μὴ ποιεῖν ἔμπροσθεν τῶν ἀνθρώπων πρὸς τὸ θεαθῆναι αὐτοῖς· εἰ δὲ μή γε, μισθὸν οὐκ ἔχετε παρὰ τῷ πατρὶ ὑμῶν τῷ ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς.
paragraphs.translit: Prosechete de tēn dikaiosynēn hymōn mē poiein emprosthen tōn anthrōpōn pros to theathēnai autois· ei de mē ge, misthon ouk echete para tō patri hymōn tō en tois ouranois.

paragraphs.text: When therefore thou doest alms, sound not a trumpet before thee, as the hypocrites do in the synagogues and in the streets, that they may have glory of men. Verily I say unto you, They have received their reward.
paragraphs.original: Ὅταν οὖν ποιῇς ἐλεημοσύνην, μὴ σαλπίσῃς ἔμπροσθέν σου, ὥσπερ οἱ ὑποκριταὶ ποιοῦσιν ἐν ταῖς συναγωγαῖς καὶ ἐν ταῖς ῥύμαις, ὅπως δοξασθῶσιν ὑπὸ τῶν ἀνθρώπων· ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, ἀπέχουσιν τὸν μισθὸν αὐτῶν.
paragraphs.translit: Hotan oun poiēs eleēmosynēn, mē salpisēs emprosthen sou, hōsper hoi hypokritai poiousin en tais synagōgais kai en tais rhymais, hopōs doxasthōsin hypo tōn anthrōpōn· amēn legō hymin, apechousin ton misthon autōn.

paragraphs.text: But when thou doest alms, let not thy left hand know what thy right hand doeth:
paragraphs.original: σοῦ δὲ ποιοῦντος ἐλεημοσύνην μὴ γνώτω ἡ ἀριστερά σου τί ποιεῖ ἡ δεξιά σου,
paragraphs.translit: sou de poiountos eleēmosynēn mē gnōtō hē aristera sou ti poiei hē dexia sou,

paragraphs.text: that thine alms may be in secret: and thy Father who seeth in secret shall recompense thee.
paragraphs.original: ὅπως ᾖ σου ἡ ἐλεημοσύνη ἐν τῷ κρυπτῷ· καὶ ὁ πατήρ σου ὁ βλέπων ἐν τῷ κρυπτῷ ἀποδώσει σοι.
paragraphs.translit: hopōs ē sou hē eleēmosynē en tō kryptō· kai ho patēr sou ho blepōn en tō kryptō apodōsei soi.

paragraphs.text: And when ye pray, ye shall not be as the hypocrites: for they love to stand and pray in the synagogues and in the corners of the streets, that they may be seen of men. Verily I say unto you, They have received their reward.
paragraphs.original: Καὶ ὅταν προσεύχησθε, οὐκ ἔσεσθε ὡς οἱ ὑποκριταί· ὅτι φιλοῦσιν ἐν ταῖς συναγωγαῖς καὶ ἐν ταῖς γωνίαις τῶν πλατειῶν ἑστῶτες προσεύχεσθαι, ὅπως φανῶσιν τοῖς ἀνθρώποις· ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, ἀπέχουσι τὸν μισθὸν αὐτῶν.
paragraphs.translit: Kai hotan proseuchēsthe, ouk esesthe hōs hoi hypokritai· hoti philousin en tais synagōgais kai en tais gōniais tōn plateiōn hestōtes proseuchesthai, hopōs phanōsin tois anthrōpois· amēn legō hymin, apechousi ton misthon autōn.

paragraphs.text: But thou, when thou prayest, enter into thine inner chamber, and having shut thy door, pray to thy Father who is in secret, and thy Father who seeth in secret shall recompense thee.
paragraphs.original: σὺ δὲ ὅταν προσεύχῃ, εἴσελθε εἰς τὸ ταμεῖόν σου καὶ κλείσας τὴν θύραν σου πρόσευξαι τῷ πατρί σου τῷ ἐν τῷ κρυπτῷ· καὶ ὁ πατήρ σου ὁ βλέπων ἐν τῷ κρυπτῷ ἀποδώσει σοι.
paragraphs.translit: sy de hotan proseuchē, eiselthe eis to tameion sou kai kleisas tēn thyran sou proseuxai tō patri sou tō en tō kryptō· kai ho patēr sou ho blepōn en tō kryptō apodōsei soi.

paragraphs.text: And in praying use not vain repetitions, as the Gentiles do: for they think that they shall be heard for their much speaking.
paragraphs.original: Προσευχόμενοι δὲ μὴ βατταλογήσητε ὥσπερ οἱ ἐθνικοί, δοκοῦσιν γὰρ ὅτι ἐν τῇ πολυλογίᾳ αὐτῶν εἰσακουσθήσονται·
paragraphs.translit: Proseuchomenoi de mē battalogēsēte hōsper hoi ethnikoi, dokousin gar hoti en tē polylogia autōn eisakousthēsontai·

paragraphs.text: Be not therefore like unto them: for your Father knoweth what things ye have need of, before ye ask him.
paragraphs.original: μὴ οὖν ὁμοιωθῆτε αὐτοῖς, οἶδεν γὰρ ὁ πατὴρ ὑμῶν ὧν χρείαν ἔχετε πρὸ τοῦ ὑμᾶς αἰτῆσαι αὐτόν.
paragraphs.translit: mē oun homoiōthēte autois, oiden gar ho patēr hymōn hōn chreian echete pro tou hymas aitēsai auton.

paragraphs.text: After this manner therefore pray ye. Our Father who art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name.
paragraphs.original: Οὕτως οὖν προσεύχεσθε ὑμεῖς· Πάτερ ἡμῶν ὁ ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς· ἁγιασθήτω τὸ ὄνομά σου,
paragraphs.translit: Houtōs oun proseuchesthe hymeis· Pater hēmōn ho en tois ouranois· hagiasthētō to onoma sou,

paragraphs.text: Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done, as in heaven, so on earth.
paragraphs.original: ἐλθέτω ἡ βασιλεία σου, γενηθήτω τὸ θέλημά σου, ὡς ἐν οὐρανῷ καὶ ἐπὶ γῆς·
paragraphs.translit: elthetō hē basileia sou, genēthētō to thelēma sou, hōs en ouranō kai epi gēs·

paragraphs.text: Give us this day our daily bread.
paragraphs.original: τὸν ἄρτον ἡμῶν τὸν ἐπιούσιον δὸς ἡμῖν σήμερον·
paragraphs.translit: ton arton hēmōn ton epiousion dos hēmin sēmeron·

paragraphs.text: And forgive us our debts, as we also have forgiven our debtors.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἄφες ἡμῖν τὰ ὀφειλήματα ἡμῶν, ὡς καὶ ἡμεῖς ἀφήκαμεν τοῖς ὀφειλέταις ἡμῶν·
paragraphs.translit: kai aphes hēmin ta opheilēmata hēmōn, hōs kai hēmeis aphēkamen tois opheiletais hēmōn·

paragraphs.text: And bring us not into temptation, but deliver us from the evil [one.]
paragraphs.original: καὶ μὴ εἰσενέγκῃς ἡμᾶς εἰς πειρασμόν, ἀλλὰ ῥῦσαι ἡμᾶς ἀπὸ τοῦ πονηροῦ.
paragraphs.translit: kai mē eisenenkēs hēmas eis peirasmon, alla rhysai hēmas apo tou ponērou.

paragraphs.text: For if ye forgive men their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you.
paragraphs.original: ἐὰν γὰρ ἀφῆτε τοῖς ἀνθρώποις τὰ παραπτώματα αὐτῶν, ἀφήσει καὶ ὑμῖν ὁ πατὴρ ὑμῶν ὁ οὐράνιος·
paragraphs.translit: ean gar aphēte tois anthrōpois ta paraptōmata autōn, aphēsei kai hymin ho patēr hymōn ho ouranios·

paragraphs.text: But if ye forgive not men their trespasses, neither will your Father forgive your trespasses.
paragraphs.original: ἐὰν δὲ μὴ ἀφῆτε τοῖς ἀνθρώποις, οὐδὲ ὁ πατὴρ ὑμῶν ἀφήσει τὰ παραπτώματα ὑμῶν.
paragraphs.translit: ean de mē aphēte tois anthrōpois, oude ho patēr hymōn aphēsei ta paraptōmata hymōn.

paragraphs.text: Moreover when ye fast, be not, as the hypocrites, of a sad countenance: for they disfigure their faces, that they may be seen of men to fast. Verily I say unto you, They have received their reward.
paragraphs.original: Ὅταν δὲ νηστεύητε, μὴ γίνεσθε ὡς οἱ ὑποκριταὶ σκυθρωποί, ἀφανίζουσιν γὰρ τὰ πρόσωπα αὐτῶν ὅπως φανῶσιν τοῖς ἀνθρώποις νηστεύοντες· ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, ἀπέχουσιν τὸν μισθὸν αὐτῶν.
paragraphs.translit: Hotan de nēsteuēte, mē ginesthe hōs hoi hypokritai skythrōpoi, aphanizousin gar ta prosōpa autōn hopōs phanōsin tois anthrōpois nēsteuontes· amēn legō hymin, apechousin ton misthon autōn.

paragraphs.text: But thou, when thou fastest, anoint thy head, and wash thy face;
paragraphs.original: σὺ δὲ νηστεύων ἄλειψαί σου τὴν κεφαλὴν καὶ τὸ πρόσωπόν σου νίψαι,
paragraphs.translit: sy de nēsteuōn aleipsai sou tēn kephalēn kai to prosōpon sou nipsai,

paragraphs.text: that thou be not seen of men to fast, but of thy Father who is in secret: and thy Father, who seeth in secret, shall recompense thee.
paragraphs.original: ὅπως μὴ φανῇς τοῖς ἀνθρώποις νηστεύων ἀλλὰ τῷ πατρί σου τῷ ἐν τῷ κρυφαίῳ· καὶ ὁ πατήρ σου ὁ βλέπων ἐν τῷ κρυφαίῳ ἀποδώσει σοι.
paragraphs.translit: hopōs mē phanēs tois anthrōpois nēsteuōn alla tō patri sou tō en tō kryphaiō· kai ho patēr sou ho blepōn en tō kryphaiō apodōsei soi.

paragraphs.text: Lay not up for yourselves treasures upon the earth, where moth and rust consume, and where thieves break through and steal:
paragraphs.original: Μὴ θησαυρίζετε ὑμῖν θησαυροὺς ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς, ὅπου σὴς καὶ βρῶσις ἀφανίζει, καὶ ὅπου κλέπται διορύσσουσιν καὶ κλέπτουσιν·
paragraphs.translit: Mē thēsaurizete hymin thēsaurous epi tēs gēs, hopou sēs kai brōsis aphanizei, kai hopou kleptai dioryssousin kai kleptousin·

paragraphs.text: but lay up for yourselves treasures in heaven, where neither moth nor rust doth consume, and where thieves do not break through nor steal:
paragraphs.original: θησαυρίζετε δὲ ὑμῖν θησαυροὺς ἐν οὐρανῷ, ὅπου οὔτε σὴς οὔτε βρῶσις ἀφανίζει, καὶ ὅπου κλέπται οὐ διορύσσουσιν οὐδὲ κλέπτουσιν·
paragraphs.translit: thēsaurizete de hymin thēsaurous en ouranō, hopou oute sēs oute brōsis aphanizei, kai hopou kleptai ou dioryssousin oude kleptousin·

paragraphs.text: for where thy treasure is, there will thy heart be also.
paragraphs.original: ὅπου γάρ ἐστιν ὁ θησαυρός σου, ἐκεῖ ἔσται καὶ ἡ καρδία σου.
paragraphs.translit: hopou gar estin ho thēsauros sou, ekei estai kai hē kardia sou.

paragraphs.text: The lamp of the body is the eye: if therefore thine eye be single, thy whole body shall be full of light.
paragraphs.original: Ὁ λύχνος τοῦ σώματός ἐστιν ὁ ὀφθαλμός. ἐὰν οὖν ᾖ ὁ ὀφθαλμός σου ἁπλοῦς, ὅλον τὸ σῶμά σου φωτεινὸν ἔσται·
paragraphs.translit: Ho lychnos tou sōmatos estin ho ophthalmos. ean oun ē ho ophthalmos sou haplous, holon to sōma sou phōteinon estai·

paragraphs.text: But if thine eye be evil, thy whole body shall be full of darkness. If therefore the light that is in thee be darkness, how great is the darkness!
paragraphs.original: ἐὰν δὲ ὁ ὀφθαλμός σου πονηρὸς ᾖ, ὅλον τὸ σῶμά σου σκοτεινὸν ἔσται. εἰ οὖν τὸ φῶς τὸ ἐν σοὶ σκότος ἐστίν, τὸ σκότος πόσον.
paragraphs.translit: ean de ho ophthalmos sou ponēros ē, holon to sōma sou skoteinon estai. ei oun to phōs to en soi skotos estin, to skotos poson.

paragraphs.text: No man can serve two masters; for either he will hate the one, and love the other; or else he will hold to one, and despise the other. Ye cannot serve God and mammon.
paragraphs.original: Οὐδεὶς δύναται δυσὶ κυρίοις δουλεύειν· ἢ γὰρ τὸν ἕνα μισήσει καὶ τὸν ἕτερον ἀγαπήσει, ἢ ἑνὸς ἀνθέξεται καὶ τοῦ ἑτέρου καταφρονήσει. οὐ δύνασθε θεῷ δουλεύειν καὶ μαμωνᾷ.
paragraphs.translit: Oudeis dynatai dysi kyriois douleuein· ē gar ton hena misēsei kai ton heteron agapēsei, ē henos anthexetai kai tou heterou kataphronēsei. ou dynasthe theō douleuein kai mamōna.

paragraphs.text: Therefore I say unto you, be not anxious for your life, what ye shall eat, or what ye shall drink; nor yet for your body, what ye shall put on. Is not the life more than the food, and the body than the raiment?
paragraphs.original: Διὰ τοῦτο λέγω ὑμῖν· μὴ μεριμνᾶτε τῇ ψυχῇ ὑμῶν τί φάγητε, μηδὲ τῷ σώματι ὑμῶν τί ἐνδύσησθε· οὐχὶ ἡ ψυχὴ πλεῖόν ἐστι τῆς τροφῆς καὶ τὸ σῶμα τοῦ ἐνδύματος;
paragraphs.translit: Dia touto legō hymin· mē merimnate tē psychē hymōn ti phagēte, mēde tō sōmati hymōn ti endysēsthe· ouchi hē psychē pleion esti tēs trophēs kai to sōma tou endymatos;

paragraphs.text: Behold the birds of the heaven, that they sow not, neither do they reap, nor gather into barns; and your heavenly Father feedeth them. Are not ye of much more value then they?
paragraphs.original: ἐμβλέψατε εἰς τὰ πετεινὰ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ ὅτι οὐ σπείρουσιν οὐδὲ θερίζουσιν οὐδὲ συνάγουσιν εἰς ἀποθήκας, καὶ ὁ πατὴρ ὑμῶν ὁ οὐράνιος τρέφει αὐτά· οὐχ ὑμεῖς μᾶλλον διαφέρετε αὐτῶν;
paragraphs.translit: emblepsate eis ta peteina tou ouranou hoti ou speirousin oude therizousin oude synagousin eis apothēkas, kai ho patēr hymōn ho ouranios trephei auta· ouch hymeis mallon diapherete autōn;

paragraphs.text: And which of you by being anxious can add one cubit unto the measure of his life?
paragraphs.original: τίς δὲ ἐξ ὑμῶν μεριμνῶν δύναται προσθεῖναι ἐπὶ τὴν ἡλικίαν αὐτοῦ πῆχυν ἕνα;
paragraphs.translit: tis de ex hymōn merimnōn dynatai prostheinai epi tēn hēlikian autou pēchyn hena;

paragraphs.text: And why are ye anxious concerning raiment? Consider the lilies of the field, how they grow; they toil not, neither do they spin:
paragraphs.original: καὶ περὶ ἐνδύματος τί μεριμνᾶτε; καταμάθετε τὰ κρίνα τοῦ ἀγροῦ πῶς αὐξάνουσιν· οὐ κοπιῶσιν οὐδὲ νήθουσιν·
paragraphs.translit: kai peri endymatos ti merimnate; katamathete ta krina tou agrou pōs auxanousin· ou kopiōsin oude nēthousin·

paragraphs.text: yet I say unto you, that even Solomon in all his glory was not arrayed like one of these.
paragraphs.original: λέγω δὲ ὑμῖν ὅτι οὐδὲ Σολομὼν ἐν πάσῃ τῇ δόξῃ αὐτοῦ περιεβάλετο ὡς ἓν τούτων.
paragraphs.translit: legō de hymin hoti oude Solomōn en pasē tē doxē autou periebaleto hōs hen toutōn.

paragraphs.text: But if God doth so clothe the grass of the field, which to-day is, and to-morrow is cast into the oven, [shall he] not much more [clothe] you, O ye of little faith?
paragraphs.original: εἰ δὲ τὸν χόρτον τοῦ ἀγροῦ σήμερον ὄντα καὶ αὔριον εἰς κλίβανον βαλλόμενον ὁ θεὸς οὕτως ἀμφιέννυσιν, οὐ πολλῷ μᾶλλον ὑμᾶς, ὀλιγόπιστοι;
paragraphs.translit: ei de ton chorton tou agrou sēmeron onta kai aurion eis klibanon ballomenon ho theos houtōs amphiennysin, ou pollō mallon hymas, oligopistoi;

paragraphs.text: Be not therefore anxious, saying, What shall we eat? or, What shall we drink? or, Wherewithal shall we be clothed?
paragraphs.original: μὴ οὖν μεριμνήσητε λέγοντες· Τί φάγωμεν; ἤ· Τί πίωμεν; ἤ· Τί περιβαλώμεθα;
paragraphs.translit: mē oun merimnēsēte legontes· Ti phagōmen; ē· Ti piōmen; ē· Ti peribalōmetha;

paragraphs.text: For after all these things do the Gentiles seek; for your heavenly Father knoweth that ye have need of all these things.
paragraphs.original: πάντα γὰρ ταῦτα τὰ ἔθνη ἐπιζητοῦσιν· οἶδεν γὰρ ὁ πατὴρ ὑμῶν ὁ οὐράνιος ὅτι χρῄζετε τούτων ἁπάντων.
paragraphs.translit: panta gar tauta ta ethnē epizētousin· oiden gar ho patēr hymōn ho ouranios hoti chrēzete toutōn hapantōn.

paragraphs.text: But seek ye first his kingdom, and his righteousness; and all these things shall be added unto you.
paragraphs.original: ζητεῖτε δὲ πρῶτον τὴν βασιλείαν καὶ τὴν δικαιοσύνην αὐτοῦ, καὶ ταῦτα πάντα προστεθήσεται ὑμῖν.
paragraphs.translit: zēteite de prōton tēn basileian kai tēn dikaiosynēn autou, kai tauta panta prostethēsetai hymin.

paragraphs.text: Be not therefore anxious for the morrow: for the morrow will be anxious for itself. Sufficient unto the day is the evil thereof.
paragraphs.original: μὴ οὖν μεριμνήσητε εἰς τὴν αὔριον, ἡ γὰρ αὔριον μεριμνήσει αὑτῆς· ἀρκετὸν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ ἡ κακία αὐτῆς.
paragraphs.translit: mē oun merimnēsēte eis tēn aurion, hē gar aurion merimnēsei hautēs· arketon tē hēmera hē kakia autēs.
